questions.text: What is the file extension for a Laravel View file?
questions.explanation: Laravel views use the Blade templating engine, so view files end in .blade.php (e.g. resources/views/welcome.blade.php). A plain .php file in resources/views still loads as a view, but Blade syntax like {{ }} and @if isn't compiled in it. .view.php and .laravel.php aren't Laravel conventions at all.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of named routes?
options: To refer to long or complex URL paths using a simpler route name
To organize route files based on the name
To limit access to routes based on the user access
To automatically shorten the URL shown in the browser
questions.explanation: A named route (->name('...')) lets you generate its URL or redirect to it by name with route('name'), so you don't hard-code the path. It doesn't organize route files (you do that by splitting routes into files or groups), it doesn't restrict access (that's middleware like auth), and it doesn't change the URL the browser shows, which is still the route's path.

questions.text: This protection helps make sure that a form request actually came from your application and not from another malicious website. It generates the hidden security token used by Laravel to validate each form submission.
questions.explanation: @csrf outputs a hidden _token input holding the session's CSRF token, which Laravel checks on every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE request. @method('PUT') adds a hidden _method field so an HTML form can send PUT/PATCH/DELETE; it has nothing to do with the token. @form and @token aren't Blade directives (the csrf_token() helper exists, but it's a function, not a directive).

questions.text: Where can you find Laravel's route definitions for web routes?
questions.explanation: Browser-facing routes (with sessions, cookies and CSRF protection) live in routes/web.php. routes/api.php is for stateless API routes, prefixed with /api. routes/api_routes.php doesn't exist, and config/ holds settings files, not routes.

questions.text: Which command installs the Laravel Installer globally using Composer?
questions.explanation: composer global require laravel/installer installs the laravel command into Composer's global bin directory, after which laravel new is available. composer install installs the packages listed in an existing project's composer.json; it doesn't take a package name like this. php require isn't a command (php runs scripts), and laravel install composer has it backwards: the laravel command doesn't exist until the installer is installed.

questions.text: What will be displayed when /user is accessed using this route?
questions.explanation: {name?} is an optional parameter. When it's missing, the closure's default value 'Guest' is used, so the response is User Guest. There's no 404 because the ? makes the parameter optional, and the ? is route syntax, never part of the value, so "User ?" can't appear. Plain "User" would only show if the default were an empty string.

questions.text: What does the regular expression constraint specify about the {code} parameter?
options: The parameter can contain numeric values only.
The parameter can contain one or more digits and a plus sign symbol.
The parameter must be in between 0 and 9 digits long.
The parameter must be exactly 9 digits long.
questions.warning: The snippet constrains 'id', but the route parameter is {code}. In real Laravel this where() wouldn't apply to {code} at all. The question means it to, so answer as if it said where('code', ...).
questions.explanation: [0-9\+] is a character class matching a single digit or a literal + (the backslash escapes the plus), and the trailing + means one or more of them. So the value may contain digits and plus signs, e.g. 123 or +63. "Numeric values only" ignores the + that the class also allows. The two length options misread [0-9]: it's a range of allowed characters (0 through 9), not a length. A length would need a quantifier like {9}.

questions.text: When was Laravel first released?
questions.explanation: Taylor Otwell released the first version of Laravel in June 2011. 2008 and 2009 are before Laravel existed, and 2012 is when Laravel 3 came out.

questions.text: What is the right way to define a comment in a blade file?
questions.explanation: Blade comments are written {{-- comment --}} and are stripped out entirely, so they never reach the browser. /* */ and // are PHP comments; in a Blade template (outside @php) they're just printed as text. An HTML comment <!-- --> still shows up in the page source, and Blade expressions inside it still run.

questions.text: Which Artisan command creates a view named greeting?
questions.explanation: php artisan make:view greeting creates resources/views/greeting.blade.php. Artisan generators all use the make: prefix, and the generator is named after what it makes (a view), so make:blade and create:blade don't exist. new isn't an Artisan command either.

questions.text: This directory/folder contains the main application code, including controllers, models, and middleware.
questions.explanation: The app directory holds the core code: app/Http/Controllers, app/Models, middleware and so on. routes holds the route definitions, config holds configuration files, and public is the web root with index.php and assets.

questions.text: How do you iterate over an array or collection in a Blade template?
questions.explanation: @foreach($items as $item) ... @endforeach mirrors PHP's foreach. @iterate and @loop aren't Blade directives (there's a $loop variable available inside @foreach, but no @loop directive). @for exists but takes a counter-style loop (@for($i = 0; $i < 10; $i++)), not as syntax.

questions.text: Who is the creator of Laravel?
questions.explanation: Taylor Otwell created Laravel. David Heinemeier Hansson created Ruby on Rails, Rasmus Lerdorf created PHP, and Fabien Potencier created Symfony.

questions.text: This is the visual representation of the data, or in other words the UI (user interface). This bit will be mostly handled by HTML/CSS. Examples of UI elements may include drop-downs, charts, text boxes and tables.
questions.explanation: In MVC, the View is the presentation layer the user sees. The Model handles the data and business logic, and the Controller handles requests and connects the two. "Resources" isn't an MVC layer; it's the name of Laravel's resources/ folder.

questions.text: Which architectural pattern does Laravel follow?
questions.explanation: Laravel follows MVC (Model-View-Controller). MVP (Model-View-Presenter) and MVA (Model-View-Adapter) are different patterns, and MMVA isn't a standard architectural pattern.

questions.text: Complete the missing syntax to redirect users to specific routes in the simplest form.
questions.explanation: ->name("add-user") gives the route a name, so you can later redirect or link to it with route('add-user') or redirect()->route('add-user') instead of the full path. where adds regex constraints to route parameters. redirect() is a helper that sends a redirect response, not a method you chain onto a route. route() is the helper you call later to use the name; it doesn't set it.

questions.text: In Laravel, what function is used to get the URL of a file like images, external CSS and JS located in the public directory?
questions.explanation: asset('css/app.css') generates a full URL to a file in public, e.g. <link href="{{ asset('css/app.css') }}">. url() builds URLs to application paths in general; asset() is the helper meant for public files. file() and public() aren't URL helpers (public_path() exists, but it returns the server's filesystem path, not a URL).

questions.text: Which of the following are advantages of using Laravel?
questions.explanation: Laravel's advantages include its expressive routing, the Eloquent ORM for working with the database, and built-in modules (authentication, validation, caching, queues, etc.). None of the others ship with it. Image manipulation needs a package such as Intervention Image. Laravel can power the API behind a mobile app, but it doesn't build native apps. There's no analytics dashboard, PHP isn't compiled into binaries for different platforms, and views are written in Blade rather than built with a drag-and-drop tool.

questions.text: Select all the correct ways to call a Laravel route:
questions.explanation: url('/path') builds a URL from a path and route('name') builds one from a named route. Route::post() defines a route rather than calling one. redirect() sends a redirect response and still needs a URL or route() to say where to go, so the quiz doesn't count it. href is an HTML attribute, not a function, get() isn't a global helper (Route::get() defines a route), and Route::to() doesn't exist.

questions.text: What will be the right syntax to call a named route?
questions.explanation: Named routes are called with route() and the route's name: route('create'). url('create') builds a URL to the path /create, which isn't this route. url('create-product') uses the view name, which has nothing to do with the URL. route('/product/create') passes a path where a name is expected, so Laravel throws a "Route not defined" error.

questions.text: Given the following constraint, which URL is invalid?
questions.explanation: The pattern allows letters, digits and underscores only. ben-gandeza contains a hyphen, which isn't in the character class, so it fails. The rest pass: BEN2027 and benjamin123 are only letters and digits, and ben_gandeza is fine because _ is allowed.

questions.text: ___ is a tool used to install Laravel, update Laravel, and bring in external dependencies.
questions.explanation: Composer is PHP's dependency manager. It installs Laravel and its packages and keeps them updated.

questions.text: What route is placed at the end of your route definitions to ensure it catches any requests/errors that haven't been handled by previous routes?
questions.explanation: Route::fallback() registers a route that runs when no other route matches, and it should be the last route registered. Route::error() and Route::catch() don't exist, with or without a '404' argument. To customize the 404 page itself, you add resources/views/errors/404.blade.php.

questions.text: Laravel folder where all of the route definitions live, both for HTTP routes and "console routes," or Artisan commands.
questions.explanation: The routes folder holds web.php, api.php and console.php (Artisan command definitions). Http is app/Http, which holds controllers and middleware. public is the web root, and artisan is the command-line script in the project root, a file rather than a folder.

questions.text: This directory houses your assets such as images, external JavaScript, and external CSS.
questions.explanation: public is the web root. It holds index.php and publicly served assets like images, CSS and JS. resources holds views and uncompiled source CSS/JS that get built into public. vendor holds Composer packages, and storage holds logs, cache and uploaded files (served only after php artisan storage:link).

questions.text: If you want to display a variable in a blade file, what will be the symbol used as a replacement for the opening and closing of PHP tags? (<?php ?>)
questions.explanation: {{ $variable }} echoes a value in Blade, escaped with htmlspecialchars. It replaces <?php echo $variable; ?>. $ is just the prefix every PHP variable has, [] is array syntax, and URL::to() generates URLs rather than displaying a variable.

questions.text: What artisan command would you use to create a new controller?
questions.explanation: php artisan make:controller UserController creates app/Http/Controllers/UserController.php. Artisan generators use the make: prefix, so new:controller, create:controller and plain controller aren't commands.

questions.text: Match each HTTP verb with its description.
questions.explanation: GET reads data, POST creates/submits it, PUT/PATCH updates it (PUT replaces, PATCH changes part), and DELETE removes it.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a directive used in Laravel Blade for switch?
questions.explanation: Blade's switch uses @switch, @case, @break, @default and @endswitch, so @break, @case and @default are all real. There is no @enddefault: the default case ends at @endswitch.

questions.text: After installing the Laravel Installer, which command can be used to create a new Laravel project?
questions.explanation: The installer provides the laravel new projectName command. php laravel projectName would try to run a PHP file named laravel. Artisan only exists inside an existing project and has no create command. Without the installer you'd use composer create-project laravel/laravel projectName; composer project isn't a command.

questions.text: It controls the data shown to the user. When a user interacts with the site/app, it will retrieve the relevant data from the model and then display it to the user using the view component.
questions.explanation: The Controller handles the request, pulls data from the Model, and passes it to the View for display. The Model represents the data itself, and the View only displays it. "Resources" isn't an MVC component.

questions.text: Where are Laravel views stored by default?
questions.explanation: Blade templates live in resources/views. public is the web root for assets, so views don't go there. app/views was the location back in Laravel 4. storage only holds the compiled copies of views (in storage/framework/views), not the templates you write.

questions.text: Which are the correct ways to pass data from a controller to a view in Laravel?
questions.explanation: view() takes an associative array of data: ['key' => $input] makes $key available in the view, and compact('input') builds ['input' => $input] from the variable's name. 'key' = $input is a syntax error, because you can't assign to a string. var() and all() aren't PHP functions for this. array('input') is just [0 => 'input'], with no usable key, and '$input' is a plain string, not an array.
